bib.title: Men Also Like Shopping: Reducing Gender Bias Amplification using Corpus-level Constraints

question: Do datasets and structured-prediction models for visual semantic role labeling and multilabel classification carry and amplify gender bias, and can corpus-level constraints reduce the amplification?
hypothesis: Datasets gathered from the web are gender biased and models trained on them amplify that bias, more so where initial bias is larger.
contributions: A framework to quantify bias and bias amplification in structured prediction
Evidence that imSitu and MS-COCO are gender biased and trained CRFs amplify the bias
RBA: corpus-level constraints solved with Lagrangian relaxation as a meta-algorithm over the original inference

method.summary: Bias score b(o,g)=c(o,g)/sum c(o,g') is compared between training labels and model predictions on held-out data. RBA adds corpus-level gender-ratio constraints (within margin gamma of training ratio) and solves by Lagrangian relaxation, re-running the original per-instance inference each iteration.
method.task: visual semantic role labeling (imSitu) and multilabel object classification (MS-COCO), bias measurement and debiasing at inference

datasets.name: imSitu
datasets.size: about 125,000 images originally (75,702 train, 25,200 dev, 25,200 test); about 60,000 after filtering to 212 human-oriented verbs
datasets.source: Yatskar et al. 2016; FrameNet verbs, WordNet nouns
datasets.preprocessing: non-human verbs (e.g. rearing, retrieving, wagging) removed, leaving 212 verbs

datasets.name: MS-COCO (multilabel)
datasets.preprocessing: gender from the five captions per image: mark man or woman if any caption mentions it, drop images mentioning both; keep objects co-occurring with man or woman at least 100 times in training

models.name: imSitu CRF
models.architecture: CRF with potentials exp(w^T f_i + b), VGG conv features
models.init_from: pretrained on the original task with 504 verbs

models.name: MS-COCO CRF
models.architecture: CRF over object categories and gender, ResNet-50 features

training.hardware: inferred: NVIDIA hardware grants acknowledged, GPU not stated

other.imSitu: uses the released baseline CRF; no training hyperparameters given

inference.decoding: argmax_y log p(y|i) with corpus-level constraints, Lagrangian relaxation
inference.samples: single run per setting; no seeds reported

parameters.constraints: applied over the whole dev or test set; constraints derived from the training set; test ground truth never used

metrics.name: mean bias amplification
metrics.definition: (1/|O|) sum_g sum_{o: b*(o,g)>1/|G|} (b~(o,g) - b*(o,g)), training vs predicted bias

metrics.name: Viol.
metrics.definition: number of verbs/objects whose predicted bias exceeds the training bias by over 0.05

metrics.name: top-1 semantic role accuracy (vSRL)
metrics.definition: how often the correct verb was predicted and noun value correctly assigned to a role

eval.protocol: dev and test sets; single run, no significance test stated

results.claim: Model predictions amplify the training gender skew for cooking (abstract example).
results.setup: imSitu vSRL, 212 verbs, VGG-feature CRF, gender binary on agent role
results.quote: the activity cooking is over 33% more likely to involve females than males in a train- ing set, and a trained model further ampli- ﬁes the disparity to 68% at test time
results.note: Quote has PDF hyphenation breaks; Fig 1 caption gives man in 33% of cooking agent roles in training and 16% after CRF.

results.claim: RBA reduces mean bias amplification on imSitu vSRL test set.
results.setup: imSitu vSRL, 212 verbs, VGG-feature CRF, gender binary on agent role, test set
results.quote: we decrease bias ampliﬁcation by 40.5% (Amp. bias)

results.claim: RBA reduces mean bias amplification on MS-COCO MLC test set.
results.setup: MS-COCO MLC, 66 objects, ResNet-50 CRF, gender from captions, test set
results.quote: we de- crease bias ampliﬁcation by 47.5% (Amp. bias)

results.claim: Over 45% of verbs and 37% of objects are biased toward one gender by more than 2:1.
results.quote: over 45% and 37% of verbs and objects, respectively, exhibit bias to- ward a gender greater than 2:1

results.claim: imSitu: 64.6% of verbs favour a male agent, average bias 0.707.
results.quote: 64.6% of verbs favoring a male agent by an average bias of 0.707

results.claim: imSitu mean bias amplification on dev is 0.050, with 45.75% of verbs amplified.
results.setup: imSitu vSRL, 212 verbs, VGG-feature CRF, gender binary on agent role, dev set
results.quote: The mean bias ampli- ﬁcation in the development set is high, 0.050 on average, with 45.75% of verbs exhibiting ampli- ﬁcation

results.claim: MS-COCO: 86.6% of objects are biased toward men, average magnitude 0.65.
results.setup: MS-COCO MLC, 66 objects, ResNet-50 CRF, gender from captions, training set
results.quote: 86.6% of ob- jects biased toward men, but with smaller average magnitude, 0.65

results.claim: MS-COCO mean bias amplification is 0.036 on dev, 65.67% of objects amplified.
results.setup: MS-COCO MLC, 66 objects, ResNet-50 CRF, gender from captions, dev set
results.quote: The mean bias ampli- ﬁca- tion across all objects is 0.036, with 65.67% of nouns exhibiting ampli- ﬁcation

results.claim: Highly biased categories amplify more: mean amplification 0.072 (vSRL) vs 0.050 overall.
results.setup: imSitu vSRL, 212 verbs, VGG-feature CRF, gender binary on agent role, dev set, training bias over 0.7
results.quote: verbs with training bias over 0.7 in either the male or female direction have a mean ampliﬁcation of 0.072

results.claim: vSRL accuracy barely changes with RBA on test set: 24.14 to 24.01.
results.setup: imSitu vSRL, 212 verbs, VGG-feature CRF, gender binary on agent role, test set, top-1 semantic role accuracy

results.claim: MLC mAP barely changes with RBA on test set: 45.40 to 45.38.
results.setup: MS-COCO MLC, 66 objects, ResNet-50 CRF, gender from captions, test set, top-1 mAP

limits: Gender binary only, as perceived by annotators; authors say finer-grained analysis needed for production.
Assumes evaluation set is identically distributed to training set, so the target ratio is the training ratio, which is itself biased.
RBA cannot remove all amplification and struggles where initial bias is low.
Unclear whether other predictors amplify more or less; only one bias measure and one CRF family tested.
Pre-LLM: CRFs over CNN features, not language models; the amplification metric and corpus-level calibration idea are what carry over.
Single run per setting, no seeds or significance tests.

terms.definition: b(o,g)=c(o,g)/sum_g' c(o,g'), the share of occurrences of output o that co-occur with demographic value g
predicted bias b~(o,g) exceeds training bias b*(o,g) where b*(o,g)>1/|G|
Reducing Bias Amplification, corpus-level constrained inference via Lagrangian relaxation
